statement: Let k, m ≥ 1, t = m+1, and k+m ≤ d−2. Let P0 be either uniform probability on Sd−1 or standard Gaussian probability on Rd, and let 14 ν = fP0 for a bounded nonnegative Borel function f. With the notation in (20) and (24), for every nonnegative Borel function H(A, y, u), Z γk,d(dA) Z Rk pA(y)t Z H(A, y, u) ν⊗t A,y(du) dy = (2π)−km/2 Z J(u)−k ν⊗t (du) Z H(A, Au1, u) γFu k,d(dA). (25) Both sides are finite measures before the test H is inserted. They are supported on Aui = y for every i, full-column-rank Du, and full-row-rank A. In the spherical case the common fiber has positive radius. Thus (25) is an identity of finite measures on (A, y, u); the right side places y at Au1. For a full-rank A, alternatively define pA(y) by the lower limit of its radius-1/n Lebesgue ball averages or by the lower limit of its Gaussian convolutions with covariance n−2Ik. Each choice is jointly measurable and agrees with (24) for Lebesgue-almost every y. All three versions agree at y = Au1, with a finite positive value, almost everywhere for the finite reference measure R(du, dA) = ν⊗t (du)γFu k,d(dA). (26) When ν = 0 the last assertion is vacuous. The equality is obtained using either ball or Gaussian approximate identities in both integration orders for the base law P0, then multiplying the resulting measure identity by the bounded density factors.
